description: Expose trustworthy Mohist server runtime information and provide a guarded local-source Update & Restart flow from Settings > System.

tasks.title: Capture stable runtime identity
tasks.description: Add a backend runtime build identity service initialized once at server startup. It should report running version, running git hash, and startup time, preferring assembly or generated metadata and falling back to local git HEAD only for source-run development mode.
acceptanceCriteria: Runtime identity is registered as a singleton and reused by all System runtime responses.
running.gitHash remains unchanged for the lifetime of the process even when the source repository HEAD changes.
Backend tests cover metadata identity and source-run git HEAD fallback.
tasks.notes: Keep MOHIST_GIT_HASH as a possible metadata input, but do not rely on it exclusively.

tasks.title: Detect trusted local-source install
tasks.description: Implement user systemd install detection for Mohist server and runner units. Classify local-source only when the trusted mohist.service unit has a WorkingDirectory containing Mohist.sln and an ExecStart source-run shape for Mohist.Server.csproj.
acceptanceCriteria: Valid local-source unit files produce install.mode = local-source and expose the trusted source path.
Missing, malformed, binary, or non-source unit shapes produce binary or unknown and do not mark update eligible.
Tests cover supported and unsupported systemd unit shapes without using real user systemd state.
tasks.output: Systemd install detector and unit parsing tests
tasks.notes: Do not accept unit names or paths from HTTP requests.

tasks.title: Inspect trusted source state
tasks.description: Add source repository inspection for the trusted install path. Each System info request should be able to read source path, branch, HEAD hash, and dirty state from the detected repository without using request-supplied paths.
acceptanceCriteria: A clean trusted repository reports source.path, source.branch, source.head, and source.dirty = false.
A dirty trusted repository reports source.dirty = true with no false update eligibility.
Tests demonstrate source.head can differ from the stable running.gitHash.
tasks.output: Git source inspector and source-state tests
tasks.notes: Use bounded process execution or an existing git abstraction; avoid exposing raw command output by default.

tasks.title: Compose System runtime info
tasks.description: Create the backend composition service and DTOs for running identity, source state, install facts, update eligibility, service state, and Mohist paths. Compute update status from trusted install facts, config gate, source cleanliness, and running/source hash comparison.
acceptanceCriteria: System info composition returns running, source, install, update, services, and paths sections with typed values.
Clean local-source installs with source.head != running.gitHash return update.status = update-available and update.available = true when enabled.
Dirty, unsupported, disabled, unknown or missing-identity, and up-to-date states return clear status and reason values.
tasks.output: SystemInfoService, DTOs, config gate, and eligibility tests
tasks.notes: Default System update to enabled only when a supported local-source development install is proven safe, or disabled otherwise.

tasks.title: Expose System info API
tasks.description: Register GET /api/system/info as the typed source of truth for Settings > System. The route should return runtime identity, dynamic source state, install mode, update eligibility, service statuses, and existing db/config/logs/opencode paths.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/system/info returns 200 with all required payload sections and fields.
Unsupported installs return update.available = false, update.status = unsupported, and a clear update.reason.
API tests cover update-available, dirty-source, unsupported, and path-field responses.
tasks.notes: Do not remove /api/status; System settings should move to this new endpoint.

tasks.title: Persist update job state
tasks.description: Add durable storage for the latest System update job outside process memory. Persist job id, status, current stage, bounded stage logs, timestamps, target source hash, and final confirmation fields so a restarted server can report the latest state.
acceptanceCriteria: Update job state can be written, read, and replaced through a backend store abstraction.
Stage logs are bounded and default status payloads do not include environment data or unbounded command output.
Tests prove latest job state survives store re-instantiation simulating process restart.
tasks.notes: Prefer the existing Mohist data directory; use JSON or SQLite according to nearby server storage conventions.

tasks.title: Run guarded local-source update job
tasks.description: Implement SystemUpdateService for the fixed local-source update flow: revalidate trusted install facts, reject dirty or unsupported state, build Mohist.sln in the trusted repo, restart mohist.service, wait for API/root/assets readiness, and restart the trusted runner unit when present. Allow only one active job at a time.
acceptanceCriteria: Eligible updates run only dotnet build Mohist.sln in the trusted detected repository and fixed user systemd restarts for trusted units.
Unsupported, dirty-source, disabled, up-to-date, and concurrent update attempts are rejected without starting build or restart commands.
Job stages include Building, Restarting server, Waiting for reconnect, Ready, failure states, and final hash confirmation when available.
Tests verify no request-supplied command, path, unit, or environment input affects execution.
tasks.output: SystemUpdateService with guarded execution and concurrency tests
tasks.notes: Abstract process/systemd/HTTP readiness operations so tests can assert the command allowlist without restarting real services.

tasks.title: Expose System update APIs
tasks.description: Register POST /api/system/update and GET /api/system/update/status. The start endpoint should ignore request execution details and return accepted job information only for eligible local-source updates; the status endpoint should return the latest durable job or a clear empty state.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/system/update returns an accepted response with jobId for an eligible update.
POST /api/system/update returns 4xx for unsupported, disabled, dirty, and up-to-date states with clear messages.
POST /api/system/update returns 409 Conflict when an update job is already running.
GET /api/system/update/status returns latest persisted job state or a clear empty state.
tasks.output: POST /api/system/update and GET /api/system/update/status endpoints with API tests
tasks.notes: Keep request body empty or ignored for execution decisions.

tasks.title: Add Web System API hooks
tasks.description: Extend the Web API client, types, and query hooks for /system/info, /system/update, and /system/update/status. Replace the placeholder rebuild mutation with a real System update mutation that surfaces backend error messages.
acceptanceCriteria: Typed Web models represent running, source, install, update, services, paths, and update job status payloads.
Settings can load System info through a query hook with loading and error states.
The update mutation calls POST /api/system/update and displays unsupported, dirty-source, conflict, and generic failures from the server.
No Web code path still invokes the intentional unsupported rebuild mutation.
tasks.output: Web System API client, hooks, and mutation tests
tasks.notes: Use the backend-provided update.status as the source of truth for eligibility messaging.

tasks.title: Render Server Runtime section
tasks.description: Update Settings > System to show the Server Runtime section using /api/system/info. Display running version/hash, source path/branch/head/dirty state, install mode, update status, server and runner service status, and existing system paths with short hashes and full hash access.
acceptanceCriteria: Settings > System renders all required runtime, source, install, update, service, and path fields from System info.
Git hashes are shortened for display while preserving access to the full value through tooltip, title, or copyable text.
Loading and error states avoid presenting unknown values as confirmed runtime facts.
Web tests cover normal runtime display and existing path visibility.
tasks.output: Settings > System Server Runtime UI and display tests
tasks.notes: Preserve the existing Settings visual language; this is an operational panel.

tasks.title: Render update eligibility states
tasks.description: Add eligibility-specific UI states for local-source update availability, unsupported deployments, dirty source, and up-to-date deployments. Rename the action to Update & Restart and show it only for eligible local-source update-available states.
acceptanceCriteria: Update & Restart appears only when install.mode = local-source, source.head differs from running.gitHash, and update.status = update-available.
Rebuild & Restart wording is removed from the System update action.
Unsupported deployments show an explanatory note and no update button.
Dirty source shows a clear warning and disables or hides the first-iteration update action.
Web tests cover eligible, unsupported, dirty, and up-to-date states.
tasks.notes: Do not duplicate server-side safety rules beyond simple display conditions.

tasks.title: Track update progress and reconnect
tasks.description: Implement the client-side update progress flow after Update & Restart. Poll update status, show Building, Restarting server, Waiting for reconnect, and Ready stages, poll health during disconnects, refetch System info/status after reconnect, and confirm success when running.gitHash equals source.head.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking Update & Restart starts a System update job and renders progress from durable update status.
The UI polls health during server restart disconnects and refetches System info plus update status after reconnect.
Success is shown only when refreshed running.gitHash equals source.head or backend final confirmation reports the same.
Reloading Settings > System during or after an update recovers and renders the latest persisted job state.
Web tests cover progress stages, reconnect polling, recovered status, and failed update messages.
tasks.output: Reconnect-aware update progress UI and tests
tasks.notes: Use polling rather than SSE for this iteration.

tasks.title: Run backend verification suite
tasks.description: Run and stabilize backend tests for the System runtime and update APIs. Ensure tests cover runtime identity, local-source detection, unsupported installs, update availability, dirty source, fixed command execution, concurrency conflict, readiness, and persisted status across restart boundary.
acceptanceCriteria: Backend test command succeeds for Mohist.Server tests relevant to System runtime/update.
All acceptance scenarios from system-runtime, http-api, and server-daemon specs have direct or integration test coverage.
No tests require real systemd service restarts or arbitrary local machine state.
tasks.notes: Use mocks/fakes for process execution, systemd, filesystem unit roots, and readiness probes.

tasks.title: Run Web verification suite
tasks.description: Run and stabilize Web tests for Settings > System runtime display and update behavior. Confirm that typed hooks, eligibility rendering, dirty/unsupported states, update progress, reconnect handling, and recovered status behave correctly.
acceptanceCriteria: Web test command succeeds for Settings > System and System API hook coverage.
Tests verify the update button appears only when eligible and never uses Rebuild & Restart wording.
Tests verify progress, reconnect/refetch, recovered status, and server-provided error rendering.
tasks.notes: Mock HTTP responses for restart disconnects and health recovery.

tasks.title: Perform integrated acceptance review
tasks.description: Perform a final implementation review against issue acceptance criteria and OpenSpec requirements. Verify task dependencies were satisfied, safety constraints remain enforced, and System settings behavior aligns with the backend contract.
acceptanceCriteria: All tasks that implement required behavior have passing verification or documented blockers.
The final implementation does not accept arbitrary command, path, unit, or environment input from Web update requests.
Settings > System can answer running version/hash, trusted source path/head/dirty state, install mode, update support, service status, and post-update confirmation.
Any remaining limitations are documented as unsupported states rather than silent failures.
tasks.notes: This task should not add new product behavior unless a review finding requires a small corrective fix.
